core_size.meaning: Line count measures source size; it does not establish feature completeness or agent quality.

failure_history: An initial agent fixture passed an unsupported overwrite argument to the create-only write tool; it was corrected before the functional suite passed.
The GUI harness encountered a detached transient Webview frame; it now selects the ready extension frame and handles detachment during polling.
A native GUI source-open probe raced a pending reload; the UI now disables operation controls immediately and the probe waits for completed reload.
A VSIX probe ambiguously matched two Enabled labels; it now targets the status badge.
The standalone editor typecheck rejected NodeList iteration without DOM.Iterable; Array.from corrected it. Check and build now use fail-fast shell execution.

A broad run loaded an earlier Core snapshot while a newly added duplicate-key test was written; that run failed and is not the final evidence. After freezing implementation, the final complete suite passed.

An actual /bin/true hook showed that a successful command closing stdin was being reported as an input failure. Closed-input handling now preserves its real exit/output and records stdin_written; final tests include this case.
limits: The 250,000-line Core target and complete upstream synthesis remain unfinished.
Host commands are not an OS sandbox; child filesystem/network effects are not individually mediated by Core read/edit/network rules.
Linux ownership covers the process group; descendants deliberately escaping it require future OS isolation. Windows direct-child cleanup is not descendant cleanup.
Replay-safe Hook declarations are explicit operator assertions, not a security guarantee. Effect barriers are scoped to one durable workflow.
Hook audit history is bounded in memory and is not durable across Core restart.
HTTP/prompt/fire-and-forget hooks, upstream dialect adapters, permission notifications, compaction lifecycle and plugin package integration remain pending.
Actual GUI evidence covers development native Workbench and VSIX Webview; no complete installer, live-model or Windows runtime verification is claimed.
